page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained vCPU configuration. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, it provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores across 2 threads per core) from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. While retaining the massive 256.0 GB RAM allocation and 1288 GB local SSD of a standard 32-vCPU chassis, it exposes only a quarter of the processor capacity. This establishes an extreme memory ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-core compute performance, reaching 2700.98 on stress-ng. However, uncached memory bandwidth falls into the lower quartile, recording 38.45 GB/sec for 256MB block reads and 22.42 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 8.17 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 9.67 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language inference with a 7B parameter model yielded 17.43 prompt tokens per second and 9.48 generation tokens per second.

The constrained CPU structure provides distinct licensing cost efficiency for software billed on a per-core basis, such as relational database engines, while offering large RAM capacity and fast local NVMe SSD storage. The key tradeoff centers on limited parallel compute power and lower uncached memory bandwidth compared to unconstrained tiers.

Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v5 is well targeted for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial working sets without heavy compute needs, including in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases like SQL Server or Oracle, and big data ETL staging environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Based on the x86_64 architecture, this constrained-core VM maintains a massive 32.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio and includes 1288 GB of local SSD storage without a discrete GPU. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates strong single-core performance (stress-ng score of 2700.98), though uncached 256MB memory throughput is comparatively low at 38.45 GB/sec read and 22.42 GB/sec write. It achieved 8.17 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.67 GB/sec in static web serving. This configuration provides significant qualitative cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that still demands extensive physical memory, making it an excellent fit for relational databases, enterprise in-memory caches, and large ETL data processing pipelines.
